claims.text: The untreated TiVNbTa alloy has a single-phase BCC dendritic microstructure.
The TiVNbTa alloy has a lower-temperature yield strength of approximately 800 MPa.
At 1273 K, untreated TiVNbTa has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa.
At 1273 K, untreated TiVNbTa has a compressive strength of approximately 423 MPa.
Adding 0.5–1.0 wt% Y2O3 nanoparticles will mitigate high-temperature softening in TiVNbTa.
Mechanical alloying of pre-alloyed TiVNbTa powder followed by spark plasma sintering at approximately 1223 K and homogenization will introduce the Y2O3 dispersion.
The proposed processing route will produce uniformly dispersed Y2O3 nano-oxides within the BCC matrix.
Y2O3 nanoparticles will remain stable and impede dislocation motion at elevated temperature.
Y2O3 nanoparticles will impede grain-boundary sliding and pin the microstructure at elevated temperature.
Suppression of dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding will counteract thermal softening of TiVNbTa.
The Y2O3-containing alloy may reach a yield strength of approximately 500 MPa or higher at 1273 K.
The Y2O3-containing alloy is predicted to have greater compressive strength than untreated TiVNbTa at 1273 K.
The strengthening improvement can be achieved while maintaining acceptable ductility.
Nonuniform Y2O3 dispersion and agglomeration may produce variable strengthening or adverse failure mechanisms.
The proposed material is intended to operate as an intermediate heat-transfer layer between W and CuCrZr at temperatures up to 1273 K under tensile and compressive loading.
